About Us: 

Founded in 2008 in Sydney, Australia, BCR is a global leader and award-winning financial services company with over 15 years of expertise and commitment to the financial services industry.


Job Summary: 

We are looking for motivated and ambitious Sales Interns to join our dynamic team in the financial services industry. This is a fantastic opportunity for individuals looking to gain hands-on experience in financial markets and develop sales skills. You’ll work closely with our experienced sales team, assisting with client outreach, market research, and lead generation while learning about financial markets, products, trading analysis and the broader financial industry as a whole.


Employment Type: Internship (Part-Time)

Duration: 4 Weeks; Mondays & Wednesdays or Tuesdays & Thursdays

Outstanding candidates will be considered for employment positions upon successful completion of the internship. Mandarin and/or English speaking preferable.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Learn about financial products and how they fit into the broader financial markets to effectively communicate with prospective clients.

  • Assist with identifying potential clients through market research and economic analysis.

  • Support the development and execution of client outreach strategies to build a pipeline of potential traders and investors.

  • Participate in client outreach to learn effective communication techniques and relationship-building strategies.

  • Provide administrative support by updating CRM systems, tracking client outreach and managing client relationships.

  • Prepare and digest market reports, economic outlooks and presentations.


Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field.

  • Strong interest in financial markets, trading, and the derivatives/CFD industry.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Self-motivated, eager to learn, and able to work both independently and as part of a team.

  • Strong organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.

  • Prior internship or sales experience in finance or related fields is a plus but not required.


What You’ll Gain:

  • Hands-on experience in the financial trading industry.

  • Exposure to financial products and market dynamics.

  • Mentorship under qualified professionals in the financial services sector.

  • Opportunity to network with key industry players.

  • Potential for future employment
94298392:
Get hands-on with real projects in CommBank’s 10-week Summer Intern Program. Learn, grow, and discover where your career can take you. 

  • Make real impact from day one - You won’t just shadow - you’ll shape! Deliver meaningful product solutions and experiences that influence how millions of individuals and businesses bank every day. 
  • Learn from the best - You’ll be supported by a dedicated Program Manager and coached by experienced product leaders. Build strong stakeholder management, strategic thinking and commercial acumen as you collaborate with teams across the business.
  • Thrive in our culture - Join a community that celebrates curiosity, creativity, and customer obsession. With wellbeing initiatives, social events, and a team that genuinely cares, you’ll do work that matters and have fun doing it.

Do work that matters  

Imagine shaping the products and experiences that millions of Australians use every day. From how customers save and invest, to how businesses grow and manage their cashflow - our products power everyday financial moments. As a Product Management Summer Intern at CommBank, you’ll connect customer need with execution and end-to-end customer experience, shaping products from idea through to delivery and continuous improvement.

Whether you're helping customers build wealth, supporting small businesses to thrive, or re-imagining how banking works in a digital world - you’ll help solve real customer problems and shape better customer experiences. Across your program, you’ll be supported to grow both deep product management capability and strong commercial acumen. You’ll learn how to think strategically, influence stakeholders, and make customer-centred decisions in a complex environment.

You’ll have access to:

  • Summer intern masterclasses and workshops
  • Learning across product management strategy, customer immersion, human centred design, risk, and commercial problem-solving
  • Coaching from experienced product leaders
  • A dedicated Program Manager and graduate buddy

See yourself in our team  

Product Managers are responsible for delivering exceptional experiences and value for our customers. It sits at the intersection of customer need, regulatory obligation, and shareholder viability.

As a CommBank Product Management Summer Intern, you will learn and grow across five core capability areas:

  • Customer – A deep customer obsession, grounded in understanding user needs and designing intuitive, seamless product experiences.
  • Data – The ability to identify critical data points and translate them into insights that guide product decisions and measure impact.
  • Industry – Subject matter knowledge of the broader market landscape, including competitors, trends, and emerging technologies relevant to the domain.
  • Business – Strong commercial acumen and an understanding of the legal, regulatory, risk, governance, and compliance frameworks that shape product strategy.
  • Product – Expertise in the product itself - its value proposition, functionality, and opportunities for innovation - ensuring it remains competitive, compliant, and aligned to customer and business needs.
     

You’ll bring your curiosity, customer centricity and creative mindset to the team. 

Our Product Management Summer Intern Programs operate within two dynamic business units: Retail Banking Services and Business Banking.

  • Retail Banking Services (Sydney) – Play a crucial role in implementing valuable changes that directly impact our retail customers and the products they use daily. This includes their savings accounts, home loans, personal loans, credit cards and investment products.
  • Business Banking (Sydney) – Gain direct exposure to the development of new propositions, product lifecycle management and uplifting our customer experiences across areas such as Digital, Payments, Everyday Business Banking, Business Lending or Customer Channels and Data.

As a Product Management Summer Intern, you’ll gain insight into how products are shaped from idea through to delivery, including how customer needs, data and design thinking inform product decisions and experiences. The program offers a unique view into how strategic decisions are made and how products evolve to enhance customer experience and financial wellbeing.

Throughout the program, you’ll have the opportunity to make a tangible difference in the lives of our customers, contributing to their financial wellbeing while building valuable product management skills in a real-world environment.

At the end of your Summer Internship, you may receive a fast-tracked offer into our 2028 Graduate Program, where you can continue to grow your career across a range of product management teams and disciplines. 

We’re interested in hearing from people who:

  • Are strong communicators who can influence and collaborate with diverse stakeholders
  • Are strategic thinkers who enjoys using data and customer insights to shape recommendations
  • Are curious, customer-obsessed and comfortable with ambiguity
  • Are strong problem solvers with a solutions mindset
  • Are adaptable, agile, and willing to think outside the box

If this sounds like you, and you are:

  • A Permanent Resident of Australia (please note, this does not include bridging visas while awaiting permanent residency or 820 visa holders), or Citizen of Australia or New Zealand at the time of your application
  • In your penultimate year of your overall university degree
  • Achieving a minimum credit average across your degree
  • Sydney based, or willing to relocate to Sydney for the program at your own expense

Apply now for our Product Management Summer Intern Program and help shape the future of banking! 

We have a long history of supporting flexible working in its many forms so you can live your best life and do your best work. Most of our teams are in one of our office locations for at least 50% of the month while working from home the rest of the time. Speak to us about how this might work in the team you're joining.  

Check out https://www.commbank.com.au/earlycareers to find out more about our pathways.

94191084:
Build your Career with an Industry Leader
 
ACCM PRIME PTY LTD is one of the global leaders in CFD broking. Since 2007, ACCM PRIME PTY LTD has remained committed to the concept of providing investors with a trading platform of authenticity and continuous creativity. We offer one-stop trading services for global investors in forex, precious metals, indices, commodities as well as various financial derivatives.


About the Internship

This internship is designed as a structured learning and training opportunity for students or recent graduates seeking exposure to the financial services industry. Interns will gain practical insights into FX trading, client relationship management, and sales processes within a professional environment.

This internship program is available in our Sydney or Melbourne offices for Mandarin-speaking candidates, while Thai and Lao-speaking candidates will be based in our Sydney office only.

Key Learning Areas & Responsibilities
Under supervision and guidance, interns will:

  • Observe and learn client communication practices via phone and email

  • Assist with preparing client service materials and responses

  • Develop an understanding of financial products and market movements

  • Support the team in client presentations and onboarding processes

  • Gain exposure to sales strategies and client relationship management

  • Learn how to monitor market trends and identify client needs


About you

  • Proficiency in Mandarin, Thai or Lao. (Requirement: Proficiency in Mandarin or Thai, with the ability to listen, speak, read, and write effectively.)

  • Currently studying or recently graduated in Business, Finance, Economics or a related discipline

  • Strong interest in financial markets and trading

  • Eagerness to learn in a professional environment

  • Good communication and interpersonal skills

  • A proactive attitude and willingness to take initiative

Internship Benefits

  • Structured training and mentorship from experienced professionals

  • Exposure to real-world financial market operations

  • Opportunity to develop practical skills in sales and client management

Internship certificate will be provided upon successful completion (subject to performance requirement)


Future Opportunities

  • Exceptional candidates may be provided with career development opportunities within the company

  • In limited cases, outstanding performers may be considered for employer-sponsored visa pathways

How to Apply
If you are passionate about financial markets and eager to gain industry exposure, we encourage you to apply.
Please submit your resume (in English, Chinese, or Thai) in PDF or Word format to:
hr@accmprime.com.au
94204286:
Company description:

Zurich is a leading multi-line insurer that serves its customers in global and local markets. With about 55,000 employees, it provides a wide range of property and casualty, life insurance products and services in more than 215 countries and territories. Zurich's customers include individuals, small businesses, and mid-sized and large companies, as well as multinational corporations.



Job description:

A new adventure awaits...

How does working for a trustworthy organisation that empowers wellbeing and is accelerating digital transformation sound like to you?

As one of Forbes 2024 ‘World's Best Employers' and Fortune's ‘World's Most Admired Companies' for 2025, Zurich - a leader in the insurance industry, is on a journey towards a brighter future… A brighter future for you - focused on your career, your wellbeing, and your community - as well as our customers and the planet.

This exciting adventure will drive positive impact. So, if you want to be part of a values led organisation, with a track record of making a real difference and continuously taking steps toward a sustainable future for our people, customers, communities, and our planet, please read on.

Let's create a brighter future together, let's make a difference

It's important to know, what you do matters. The way we work continues to evolve and at Zurich we are committed to creating new ways of working that ensure you are helping to create a brighter future.

We're thrilled to open applications to invite a new cohort of summer interns to Zurich this year into our Group Insurance team. This is a pilot program for Group Insurance, following the successful introduction of our Actuarial and Technology Summer internship programs in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Our 8-week program* will see you partner with experienced leaders and work with brilliant teams across our Group Insurance business, and namely our Product, Corporate and Partnership teams. You'll be given full support, training, and guidance, as you support real work across the business and work towards delivering a customized project aligned with your development goals. This is a paid internship based out of our head office in North Sydney.

Important to your success - let's grow together

  • You must be in your second last year of a university undergraduate or postgraduate degree.
  • A strong academic record with a credit average, or above. Please include / attach your transcript with your application.
  • You will ideally be studying Business/Commerce, Medical, Actuarial or Design.
  • You must be a permanent resident of Australia, or citizen of Australia or New Zealand and be living in Australia when you apply with us.

Belong. Zurich is here to support you

There are many reasons why Zurich is the right choice for you, but here are just a few - grow, and thrive in your career (we support and encourage it); work with global, diverse, and inclusive teams; explore your passions, fuel innovation, drive equity, collaborate and make a positive difference beyond your role; access programs to stay healthy and feel healthier; Flexwork@Zurich; become an activist in your community with the support of Z Zurich Foundation; award winning training programs; state-of-the-art Green Star rated office in North Sydney; we plant a tree for every new employee - one of many local initiatives driving our contribution to ambitious global sustainability targets. Not to mention our various employer of choice awards/memberships - WGEA; Family Inclusive workplace; Gold AWEI employer, Pride in diversity… to name a few.

We could go on, but the main point is that Zurich is a place that you can truly belong and thrive!

So, if you want to come on an adventure that will build a brighter future together, and feel a sense of togetherness, then please apply today to start your adventure!

Applications close - 7th September 2026

Zurich is an equal opportunity employer.  We are committed to ensuring that our recruitment process is fair and accessible for all candidates. If you require any special accommodations to participate in our recruitment process, we encourage you to let us know at the time of your application.

Please visit our careers page for further information on the internship program and working at Zurich. https://www.zurich.com.au/about/careers.html

*Our Summer Internship program to take place between the start of December - February, with some level of flexibility on dates and a likely office shutdown period for the Christmas and NY break (~1- 2 weeks).

Summary
The people here at Apple don’t just build products, we build the kind of wonder that revolutionize entire industries. Imagine what you could do here!

Do you have a passion for understanding how each line of code affects all the others? In the Core Operating Systems group ensuring the OS is inseparable from each device’s identity as a whole. That’s because this group is committed to building fully integrated operating systems that combine hardware, software, and apps into a single Apple experience. Your dedication to cross-disciplinary collaboration will help develop ground-breaking technologies, such as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS. By crafting these distinct, holistic user experiences, you’ll continue to uphold and advance the excellence people expect from Apple devices.

We are seeking enthusiastic engineering students to work on Apple’s operating systems, including the kernel, runtime, and low-level system services. We work on core technology that powers Apple’s operating systems, including iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, as well as subsystems such as the Secure Enclave Processor OS.

Description

Design and implementation of secure operating systems, including kernel, runtime, and system services. Work with multi-functional teams to bring up, test, debug, and verify software for new platforms and products. Contribute to security requirements and features for future hardware.

Minimum Qualifications

* Currently pursuing Bachelor's or Master’s degree in computer science or related fields.
* Able to commit to a 4-months of internship, preferably starting in January 2027.
*

Preferred Qualifications

* Background in operation systems development. This may include areas such as the kernel, low-level runtime, system services, driver frameworks, and component models.
* Understanding of system construction principles in the context of a microkernel-based environment.
* Understanding of computer architecture - how CPUs, memory, caches, and interrupts behave in response to code running at the instruction level.
* Proficiency in languages commonly used in systems, such as C.
* Habitual practice of good software engineering principles, such as using type systems, identification and prevention of undefined behaviour, property-based testing, and formal verification. Keen eye for security flaws such as buffer overruns.
* Strong communication and collaboration skills, working within an established team and with people across different teams.

Get hands-on with real projects in CommBank’s 10-week Summer Intern Program. Learn, grow, and discover where your career can take you. 

  • Make real impact from day one - You won’t just shadow - you’ll shape! Deliver meaningful product solutions and experiences that influence how millions of individuals and businesses bank every day. 
  • Learn from the best - You’ll be supported by a dedicated Program Manager and coached by experienced product leaders. Build strong stakeholder management, strategic thinking and commercial acumen as you collaborate with teams across the business.
  • Thrive in our culture - Join a community that celebrates curiosity, creativity, and customer obsession. With wellbeing initiatives, social events, and a team that genuinely cares, you’ll do work that matters and have fun doing it.

Do work that matters  

Imagine shaping the products and experiences that millions of Australians use every day. From how customers save and invest, to how businesses grow and manage their cashflow - our products power everyday financial moments. As a Product Management Summer Intern at CommBank, you’ll connect customer need with execution and end-to-end customer experience, shaping products from idea through to delivery and continuous improvement.

Whether you're helping customers build wealth, supporting small businesses to thrive, or re-imagining how banking works in a digital world - you’ll help solve real customer problems and shape better customer experiences. Across your program, you’ll be supported to grow both deep product management capability and strong commercial acumen. You’ll learn how to think strategically, influence stakeholders, and make customer-centred decisions in a complex environment.

You’ll have access to:

  • Summer intern masterclasses and workshops
  • Learning across product management strategy, customer immersion, human centred design, risk, and commercial problem-solving
  • Coaching from experienced product leaders
  • A dedicated Program Manager and graduate buddy

See yourself in our team  

Product Managers are responsible for delivering exceptional experiences and value for our customers. It sits at the intersection of customer need, regulatory obligation, and shareholder viability.

As a CommBank Product Management Summer Intern, you will learn and grow across five core capability areas:

  • Customer – A deep customer obsession, grounded in understanding user needs and designing intuitive, seamless product experiences.
  • Data – The ability to identify critical data points and translate them into insights that guide product decisions and measure impact.
  • Industry – Subject matter knowledge of the broader market landscape, including competitors, trends, and emerging technologies relevant to the domain.
  • Business – Strong commercial acumen and an understanding of the legal, regulatory, risk, governance, and compliance frameworks that shape product strategy.
  • Product – Expertise in the product itself - its value proposition, functionality, and opportunities for innovation - ensuring it remains competitive, compliant, and aligned to customer and business needs.
     

You’ll bring your curiosity, customer centricity and creative mindset to the team. 

Our Product Management Summer Intern Programs operate within two dynamic business units: Retail Banking Services and Business Banking.

  • Retail Banking Services (Sydney) – Play a crucial role in implementing valuable changes that directly impact our retail customers and the products they use daily. This includes their savings accounts, home loans, personal loans, credit cards and investment products.
  • Business Banking (Sydney) – Gain direct exposure to the development of new propositions, product lifecycle management and uplifting our customer experiences across areas such as Digital, Payments, Everyday Business Banking, Business Lending or Customer Channels and Data.

As a Product Management Summer Intern, you’ll gain insight into how products are shaped from idea through to delivery, including how customer needs, data and design thinking inform product decisions and experiences. The program offers a unique view into how strategic decisions are made and how products evolve to enhance customer experience and financial wellbeing.

Throughout the program, you’ll have the opportunity to make a tangible difference in the lives of our customers, contributing to their financial wellbeing while building valuable product management skills in a real-world environment.

At the end of your Summer Internship, you may receive a fast-tracked offer into our 2028 Graduate Program, where you can continue to grow your career across a range of product management teams and disciplines. 

We’re interested in hearing from people who:

  • Are strong communicators who can influence and collaborate with diverse stakeholders
  • Are strategic thinkers who enjoys using data and customer insights to shape recommendations
  • Are curious, customer-obsessed and comfortable with ambiguity
  • Are strong problem solvers with a solutions mindset
  • Are adaptable, agile, and willing to think outside the box

If this sounds like you, and you are:

  • A Permanent Resident of Australia (please note, this does not include bridging visas while awaiting permanent residency or 820 visa holders), or Citizen of Australia or New Zealand at the time of your application
  • In your penultimate year of your overall university degree
  • Achieving a minimum credit average across your degree
  • Sydney based, or willing to relocate to Sydney for the program at your own expense

Apply now for our Product Management Summer Intern Program and help shape the future of banking! 

We have a long history of supporting flexible working in its many forms so you can live your best life and do your best work. Most of our teams are in one of our office locations for at least 50% of the month while working from home the rest of the time. Speak to us about how this might work in the team you're joining.  

Check out https://www.commbank.com.au/earlycareers to find out more about our pathways.

About Us

PARts Australia is a data specialist developing technology and analytics to service the global requirements of the automotive industry. We develop and maintain data stores, e-commerce and web-based software solutions, including cutting-edge SaaS and cloud applications for the global automotive aftermarket and consumers. Our products are used by leading industry players including manufacturers, and are integrated with well-known systems and platforms like eBay and e-commerce system integrators.

About the Role

We're looking for two engineers to become automotive data subject matter experts — learning our business from the ground up by doing the real customer data work that keeps it running.

Your main focus is helping our customers articulate, present and publish auto parts product and fitment data for millions of parts and catalogue records online. That could mean global marketplaces, local outlets, or their own websites here and internationally.

You'll work with PARts Data Suppliers (manufacturers and brands like ARB, DBA, Gates, NGK and Ryco) and Data Users (eBay, Automotive Superstore, Repco) to understand and meet their data needs in our system.

Each position reports to one of our Product Managers — one supporting our Platform stream, one supporting our Integrations stream — with day-to-day tasking and quality assurance in our broader subject matter expert team.

This is not a software development role — we're looking for engineers who love the automotive industry. You will, however, work hands-on with data and software: running SQL-based data tasks, validating outputs, and generally getting involved with our system operations and platform development.

  • Customer data delivery — analysing what customers need from their data, then scoping, tracking and delivering it. This includes executing Customer Data Requests, bulk data tasks run against the database using prescribed scripts, progressing through our training stages under supervision.

  • Catalogue data — working with product and fitment data across the standards the industry runs on (TecAlliance/TecDoc, ACES/PIES and proprietary formats) and learning how data maps across them.

  • Customer support — helping triage and resolve customer data queries through the PARts Help Desk, handling first-level requests with guidance and escalating the complex ones.

  • Data quality — reviewing data against established thresholds, cross-referencing between standards, and flagging anomalies before they reach a customer.

  • Project coordination — helping supervise data entry resources and tools, and keeping processing and publication workflows on time.

  • Documentation — keeping runbooks and process guides current as workflows evolve, so what you learn stays transferable across the team.

This internship should ideally lead to a full-time position after study, or continued part-time work while you finish.   • Experience with databases and data analysis using Excel, SQL or other organised data structures

  • Exposure to the automotive aftermarket parts industry

Resilia is a psychological rehabilitation provider created to address the increasing complexity of psychological presentations in return-to-work claims. Upholding the belief that work should positively impact wellbeing, our experienced team have crafted best-in-class support services ensuring employees from all backgrounds thrive in the workplace and employer representatives themselves feel supported as they mitigate and manage complex mental health presentations within their organisation. 

Delivering unwavering quality, holistic support and seasoned expertise, we look to bring in Psychologist’s and Rehabilitation Counselling possessing of a growth mindset to work closely within our supportive team to ensure quality return-to-work outcomes. 

The role 
 
Our Recovery Specialists are responsible for providing specialist psychological recovery and rehabilitation services to workers/employees with psychological illness or injuries. Your career will be nurtured by working with a strong and supportive team of well-respected industry leaders and subject matter experts. 
 
Key responsibilities: 
  • Managing a case load of rehabilitation files may include various services; Same Employer / RTW cases, Vocational Assessments and Counselling, Rehabilitation Counselling, Job Seeking Education, Vocational Re-training, Workplace Assessments, Psychologic Capacity Evaluations. 
  • Administer relevant psychological and vocational inventories, score test and interpret test results. 
  • Attend case conferences with treating medical/allied health professionals to identify barriers and develop a plan for progression, based on shared goals, monitoring and case reviews. 
  • Provide workers with job seeking assistance with the assistance of ESC services where available; 
  • Assist clients with job skills training to enable them to exercise an appropriate level of independence in choosing and finding employment. 
  • Maintain regular liaison with clients and key stakeholders in performing vocational rehabilitation and counselling activities. 
  • Maintain up to date client records, including case notes and progress reports.  
What’s on offer:
  • Excellent remuneration on offer plus achievable bonus 
  • All travel reimbursed at $0.99 per km, including tolls and parking expenses 
  • Structured induction and on-boarding with buddy system, including ongoing weekly and monthly team meetings to support your learning 
  • Professional development opportunities – internal training programs for leadership and management 
  • Latest technology with laptop and iPhone provided  
  • Regular seasonal social events throughout the year 
  • Annual Christmas party 
  • Opportunity to participate in our Emerging Leaders Program for career development opportunities 
Your Wellbeing our Heartbeat - Our employee benefits program    
  • Wellbeing Support - Employee Assistance Programs, health insurance packages, gym partnership 
  • Employee Connection - Social entertainment budgets  
  • Life Balance - Unplug agreement, flexible working arrangements  
  • Paid Parental Leave - entitlements to support your growing family  
  • Learning and Development - Group supervision sessions, quarterly formal professional development and monthly bites and insights  
Who will thrive in this role? 
 
We work to our client’s pace, and in the psychological injury rehabilitation world, that’s fast, so you will be someone that can actively manage a full case load. You’ll be able to do this because your team is psychologically safe and work together to remain at the forefront of our industry. In our team, everyone is allowed to be heard and influence the direction and growth of our business. 
 
You’ll love working in a flat hierarchy where you are provided with ongoing support and mentoring to further expand your experience and discover areas of psychology and consulting that align to your strengths. 
 
If you crave purpose, flexibility, creativity, high standards and working within an agile team delivering excellence in consulting, this is the role for you. It’s time to nurture your career. 
 
Essential criteria 
  • Registration with AHPRA or Australian Society of Rehabilitation Counsellors (ASORC)
  • Previous workplace rehabilitation experience highly regarded 
  • Drivers License and access to a reliable vehicle
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, with the ability to develop and build positive relationships within a corporate environment 
  • Demonstrated organisational and time management skills 
  • Preference for an agile way of work 
  • Possessing a growth mindset 
  • The capacity to work independently and as part of a team   
Resilia is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, cultural or linguistic background, religion, disability, personal identity, veteran status, or Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. We are committed to providing a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace for all employees. 
 
Next Steps 
 
Opportunities like this won’t stick around long! If this sounds like your next rewarding role, feel free to reach out directly for a chat or apply through the "Apply" button, and we’ll be in touch to discuss further.  
  
Careers@ws-grp.com.au or call Tara 0429370805

  • Salary: HEW level 1 $63,646-$66,176, plus super & leave loading


About the Ignite Indigenous Traineeship Program
The Ignite Indigenous Traineeship Program provides Indigenous peoples of Greater Western Sydney with the opportunity to gain on-the-job training alongside vocational education and training (VET) in a large higher education organisation.

Further information on the Ignite Indigenous Traineeship Program is available at: www.westernsydney.edu.au/indigenousemployment  

About the Role
As a Business Administration Trainee, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on administration experience within a business environment while undertaking VET studies over a 12-month period. The main aspects of the role will include:

  • Completing a Certificate III in Business
  • Providing service/administrative support to the workplace supervisor and business unit 
  • Maintaining record keeping and filing systems 
  • Using computerised information systems and related technologies  
  • Prioritising own and other adhoc tasks to meet required deadlines 
  • Working collaboratively with your workplace supervisor and colleagues 
  • Building and maintaining professional workplace relations with internal and external stakeholders 


There are multiple full-time, fixed term roles on offer for 12-months, commencing in 2027.

These positions will be based in the multiple Schools, Divisions and or Institutes across Western Sydney University. Please note that some of these roles may be shared between two or more of business units within the university, and a trainee may need to travel between campuses.

There are multiple opportunities at the following Western Sydney University campuses, as below:

Campbelltown:
Faculty of Health: Join the Faculty of Health at our Campbelltown campus and gain valuable office administration experience. You'll support staff and students by coordinating meetings and events, managing enquiries, maintaining records, and preparing documents in a busy and supportive health education environment. This role is ideal for someone with an interest in health, education, and supporting future health professionals.

Hawkesbury
Office of People & Culture: Based at our Hawkesbury campus, you’ll gain hands-on experience supporting initiatives that help create a positive, inclusive and engaging staff experience across the University. Your first rotation will be with our Diversity, Equity & Inclusion team, supporting activities and events that build inclusion and belonging across Western. You’ll gain practical experience in areas such as event support, communications, resource preparation, data and reporting, and general administration, with opportunities to contribute to a range of people and culture initiatives thereafter.

Office of Future Student Engagement: Join a team dedicated to inspiring future students to explore higher education opportunities. Based at our Hawkesbury Campus, the trainee will support domestic student recruitment, widening participation and engagement activities & events. The role offers hands-on experience in administration, event coordination, presentations, project support, room bookings, and stakeholder engagement.

Kingswood
Division of Education and Students: Located at our Kingswood campus, you’ll gain hands-on experience supporting Learning and Teaching initiatives across the University, including events such as the learning and teaching showcase and professional learning activities. Develop practical skills in event and project coordination, administration, communications, data management, and stakeholder engagement while contributing to initiatives that support teaching practice and the student learning experience.

Division of Indigenous Leadership: This position sits with the Badanami Team at Kingswood and Parramatta Campuses. There are also other opportunities to work from other WSU Campuses where Badanami centres are located. You will play a key role in supporting Indigenous student success through exciting events, engagement activities and academic support programs while developing valuable skills in communications, project coordination, administration and stakeholder engagement. This is a fantastic opportunity to build your professional experience, connect with students and contribute to a culturally safe and supportive university environment.

Faculty of Engineering, Computing & Science (ECS): This position is based in Kingswood with the options to work from Parramatta South and Parramatta (Hassall St) campuses to work amongst different areas of the faculty. You will gain experience in event coordination, communications, student engagement and mentoring while helping create a culturally safe and supportive learning environment. 

ASPIRE™:  This position can be based in Campbelltown or Kingswood depending on applicant preference. In this role you will work on the ASPIRE™ Program supporting current Indigenous students with paid internship opportunities. You will gain experience in event coordination, communications, student engagement and mentoring while helping create a culturally safe and supportive learning environment.

Parramatta City
The College: Based at our Parramatta City campus, you'll support students on their journey at Western. Gain practical experience managing records, coordinating meetings and events, preparing documents and correspondence, and providing administrative support to a busy team.

Parramatta South:
Faculty of Social Sciences, Arts, Business, Education and Law (SABEL): Located at our Parramatta South campus, you'll gain hands-on experience supporting the daily operations of one of the University's largest faculties. Duties include administration, event coordination, record management, preparing documentation, and assisting staff, students, and visitors.

Division of the Provost: Based at our Parramatta South campus, you'll work within a central division that supports the University's academic faculties and schools. Gain exposure to university-wide operations in a senior executive office while developing practical skills in administration, calendar management, event coordination, communication and stakeholder support.

Applicants will be asked to rank the above opportunities across the Western Sydney University campuses in order of preference as part of the application process.

For further information, please refer to the Position Description.

About You
To be considered for this opportunity, you must:

  • Identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Person.
  • Have completed a year 9 level of schooling or equivalent.
  • Have an interest in general business administration duties.
  • Display a commitment to enrol and complete a Certificate III in Business (Administration) traineeship for 12 months.
  • Must not have completed any formal education or training resulting in a qualification.


For appointment to the position with The College, it is a mandatory requirement for the incumbent of this position to have a current NSW Employee Working with Children Clearance in accordance with the NSW Child Protection (Working with Children) Act 2012.

Benefits
We invest in the people who make our mission possible. Alongside a rewarding career, we offer a range of benefits designed to support your financial, personal and family wellbeing.

  • Community and Connection: Be part of a vibrant Indigenous community with opportunities to connect through staff networks, mentoring, cultural events and Indigenous-led initiatives.
  • Paid Cultural and Ceremonial Leave: Indigenous employees are entitled to 5 days of paid leave and 10 days of unpaid leave each year to participate in cultural and ceremonial activities and fulfil community obligations.
  • Culturally Responsive Wellbeing Support: Access dedicated wellbeing services, including culturally responsive Employee Assistance Program support Indigenous employees and their families.
  • Flexible Work and Exceptional Benefits: Enjoy flexible work arrangements, Fitness Passport, generous leave provisions, staff discounts and access to a wide range of University facilities and services.


Application Timeline

  • Advertisement: The job posting will be closing at 11:59pm on Thursday 8th October 2026.
  • Shortlisting: Following the application closing date, all applications will go through a shortlisting process, which can take up to 2 weeks.
  • Interviews: Interviews will take place on the 13th & 14th October 2026. All interviews will be conducted in a face-to-face setting on our Parramatta South Campus.  
  • Commencement: The successful applicants will commence in February 2027. 


Position Enquiries: Please contact Brody O’Brien at B.O’Brien@westernsydney.edu.au for any questions about the position. Please include the job reference code REF1833A in your email.

How to Apply: Please note that only applications submitted via the University’s online recruitment system will be considered. As part of your online application, you will be asked to respond to screening questions addressing the key qualifications, experiences and skills required for this position.

Belonging at Western
We are committed to substantive equality as outlined in our Equal Opportunity Policy. We actively encourage applications from Indigenous Australians, candidates of all gender identities and expressions, people of all abilities, and those from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

For reasonable adjustments during the application process, please contact talentacquisitionteam@westernsydney.edu.au.

About Western
This is your opportunity to be part of something bigger. By joining Western Sydney University, you become a valued member of our community. As our region changes, so too does our university. Western is boldly different, energetic, global, diverse, dynamic, and youthful.

Our mission is to deliver student success, impactful research, and stronger communities. As part of our team, you will have a stake in shaping the future of education, broadening horizons, and changing lives. Making a difference starts at Western.

For the latest please visit our website and LinkedIn.

Group Overview

The TP ICAP Group is a world leading provider of market infrastructure.

Our purpose is to provide clients with access to global financial and commodities markets, improving price discovery, liquidity, and distribution of data, through responsible and innovative solutions.

Through our people and technology, we connect clients to superior liquidity and data solutions.

The Group is home to a stable of premium brands. Collectively, TP ICAP is the largest interdealer broker in the world by revenue, the number one Energy & Commodities broker in the world, the world’s leading provider of OTC data, and an award winning all-to-all trading platform.

Founded in London in 1866, the Group operates from more than 60 offices in 28 countries. We are 5,300 people strong.  We work as one to achieve our vision of being the world’s most trusted, innovative, liquidity and data solutions specialist.


TP (Tullett Prebon)

A world-leading intermediary in the wholesale financial and energy markets, Tullett Prebon seeks to maximise value for its clients' trading activities across voice, hybrid and pure electronic channels.

We offer broking services for a wide range of asset classes, including Equities, Credit, FX, Rates and Insurance Derivatives. 

Across all asset classes, Tullett Prebon offers e-solutions to give clients the choice to enter prices and execute trades electronically and directly via one of our hybrid electronic trading systems, or to engage with brokers to help identify and negotiate trades.


Role Overview

Located in Sydney, this is a fantastic opportunity to learn broking from the ground up, to develop a long term and rewarding career on the FX Forwards Desk.  The Fwds desk focuses on the fixing of exchange rates for a particular date in the future and is used to hedge foreign currency risk.  As a trainee, you will have the opportunity to understand how the FWDS desk act as an intermediary facilitating Forward FX trades in the wholesale financial markets. This will include transacting daily trades between commercial and investment banks. Trainees will also learn how banks use FWD FX as a hedging and trading tool.

Role Responsibilities

·         Promote Tullett Prebon as a company

·         Provide complete support to the brokers for the smooth running of the desk

·         Ensure timely input of trades into trading systems

·         Resolve any trade queries received internally and externally, and ensure any trade discrepancies are resolved in a timely manner

·         Keep trade records up to date.

·         Update real-time manual / electronic whiteboards with market data

·         Provide input on various projects for brokers and traders

·         Provide live quotes through the link line to our internal regional offices

·         Monitor markets and follow financial news and developments

·         Understand the underlying products being traded and keep up to date with knowledge of new products/procedures

·         Manage the on-boarding of new clients with the Client On-Boarding team

What to expect

In the first three months, you’ll develop an understanding of the requirements of the role and begin to support our senior brokers.   You’ll be creating reports, using our company systems and providing updates from those systems to the senior brokers.  You’ll be booking trades and sending confirmations.

Within six months, you’ll be assisting with inbound queries from existing clients, the onboarding of new clients along with attending client visits.  You’ll be researching prospective customers and making outbound sales calls to prospective customers, analysing data and supporting the desk..

Beyond six month, who knows, with attention and enthusiasm, the sky is the limit.

Experience / Competences

  • You’ll have excellent communication skills, and proven ability to build rapport and develop relationships. 

  • You’ll have superb attention to detail and be able to manage multiple tasks within strict timeframes.  

  • You’ll be adept at working with  and contributing to a team and a  have a willingness to learn.

  • You will be ambitious in nature, hungry to succeed but not at the expense of your team’s success

  • You’ll always act with integrity and ethics.

Highly desirable would be experience in a sales roles or in a capacity that focuses on relationship building.  A degree in economics, finance or commerce is welcome but not essential.
